correctness.rationale: Exact signed Hessian multipliers yield a fair log-magnitude random walk. Ballot/Catalan counts prove a.s. first hit and the heavy tail, while countably many disjoint expansion-then-contraction paths yield squared stopped outputs at least 4^h x0² with probability 2^{-(2h+1)}. Summation proves infinite square expectation and the finite-cap lower bound. All quantifiers and the cap/output indexing match Algorithm 2; 201 exact finite checks replay from package. The finite checks are not a proof of infinity.

value.rationale: The counterexample turns the source’s practical cap-for-robustness choice into an exact mathematical boundary: without it, a.s. stopping coexists with both infinite mean sampling cost and infinite expected objective on a strongly convex example; a cap produces a quantified growing risk lower bound. Stable full-gradient descent at the same step rules out a merely ill-posed objective. Restricted step size and single-epoch regime are explicit.
